locator.text: Display 109.1, p. 109, in the proof of Proposition 9.6

evidence: paper: M_e = \int_0^\infty r^e F_e(r)\, dr, \qquad \sigma_e(r) = -r^{-e}\int_0^r (r')^e\bigl(F_e(r') - b_e(r')\,M_e\bigr)\, dr'.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean states the paper's display literally, in the paper's own physical variables: `physicalSigma_eq_negative_primitive` (SignedStressPrimitive.lean:719) is σ_e(r) = −(∫_0^r (r')^e · physicalAdjusted) / r^e with `physicalAdjusted = F − physicalBump` and `physicalBump P e q F z = physicalDensity P e q z * mass e F z.2`, i.e. F_e − b_e M_e. Same minus sign, same outer r^{-e}, same limits 0..r, and the b_e it subtracts is `physicalDensity P e q z = momentDensity P e (r/√q) / (√q)^{e+1}`, which is literally the paper's q^{-(e+1)/2} b̂_e(r/√q) with lengthScale = √q. The docstring at :717 says as much ('No fixed-Q chart enters this definition or identity'). The band-coordinate version `sigma_eq_negative_primitive` (:272) is the same identity in the rescaled chart; `physicalSigma` is defined from it by `physicalSigma = lengthScale q · sigma P e (nativeSource q F) (r/√q, ·)` (:598), and :719 discharges the rescaling by `interval_dilate_weighted`. This physical layer is the one the cycle consumes: `SignedMeanGain.removedBump G e f` is `physicalBump G.patch e (coordinateQ G.coord) (torusAverage (f n))` and `SignedMeanGain.physicalSigma G e f` is `physicalBarSigma = physicalSigma ∘ torusAverage` (SignedMeanGain.lean:687-693; `physicalBarSigma_eq_negative_primitive` at SignedStressPrimitive.lean:880 is the same formula on the torus average). One convention remains: M_e, where Lean's `mass e F = ∫_ℝ r^e F(r,·) dr` runs over the whole line and the paper's over (0,∞); they agree because F is radially supported in [P.a, P.b] with P.a > 0, and the repository uses exactly that bridge (`IntegratedMeanBalances.positive_integral_eq_integral`, invoked at SignedStressPrimitive.lean:314 and :142). The normalisation ∫ x^e b̂_e(x) dx = 1 the paper imposes on the profile is `momentDensity_positive_moment` (:140). No constant, exponent, sign or limit of integration differs.
